Anna: Heads-up — observed a noisy tenant in the us-west shared-gpu pool this morning. Their long chat/streaming workloads saturated the pool and bumped 95th and 99th latency for small interactive tenants.
Mateo: Oof. Any spikes in eviction/retries?
Anna: yeah, small but visible: ~8% increase in preemptions and a bunch of queued short requests timed out. CPU on control plane stayed fine; it's the GPU queues that backed up.
Kai: Do we have recent per-tenant token usage graphs? Could be a scheduler bug or just one tenant being very bursty. :thinking:
Anna: Putting a quick summary: tenant-a had sustained 20x their usual concurrent streams for 12m; tail latency for other tenants in same pool rose from 120ms p95 to 680ms p95.
Jess: Yikes. What's the mitigation plan? Short-term we can isolate tenant-a to a dedicated pool, but that costs $$ and we don't want to do that manually every time.
Mateo: I'd rather experiment with admission-control changes first — something that enforces soft fairness without hard-preempting immediately. Anna, you mentioned 'leasewise soft-quota' in the thread title?
Anna: yep — idea is to issue short GPU 'leases' (e.g., 30s slots) per tenant based on a sliding credit window. If a tenant uses >X concurrent leases over short windows, we slow their new requests (adaptive backoff) instead of bluntly evicting. Credits decay slowly so burstiness is allowed but sustained hogging is penalized.
Kai: Sounds promising. How does it interact with our existing prefix/KV cache and batching? We don't want to penalize tenants that benefit others via caching.
Anna: Plan is to weight leases by effective cache-hit contribution: if a request uses cached KV or has high batching efficiency, it costs less lease credit. That incentivizes cache-friendly patterns.
Mateo: Nice. Can we prototype as a simulation first? Feed trace of last 7 days and compare current soft-throttle vs leasewise. Metrics to compare: p50/p95 latency for small tenants, token cost, number of preemptions, fairness index (e.g., Jain's), and queue depth.
Jess: Also track rollback triggers: if p50 for any SLA-critical tenant increases >15% over baseline, abort rollout.
infra-bot: [deploy-sim-run] simulation job queued: sim-leasewise-1874021123 (trace=us-west-2026-03-16..2026-03-23)
Anna: I'm sketching a minimal admission-controller config to run in sim mode — it exposes lease_duration, window_size, base_credit, and cache_weight. Mateo, Kai — please review:
Anna: ```json
{
  "admission_controller": "leasewise",
  "lease_duration_s": 30,
  "window_s": 120,
  "base_credit": 10,
  "burst_multiplier": 3,
  "decay_half_life_s": 600,
  "cache_weight": 0.4,
  "backoff_policy": "additive-then-multiplicative",
  "penalty_threshold": 0.8
}
```
Kai: Quick question: how do we measure 'cache contribution' at admission time? We only know hit after request completes.
Anna: good catch — use an eligibility heuristic (request size + prefix match) and apply an optimistic discount; then adjust accounting retroactively when completion event arrives. That means we need to support retroactive credit reconciliation in sim.
Mateo: That's doable in sim. For production we'd need fast async accounting to avoid blocking admission path.
Jess: For rollout, sug: sim -> canary 5% of us-west pool -> 25% -> full, with realtime metrics and auto-rollback on SLA breach. Also add a kill-switch to disable retroactive reconciliation if it causes instability.
Anna: Agreed. Also need cost model: if we throttle aggressively we might bump egress (more retry loops) or push customers to Dedicated. We'll include token-cost per tenant in sim output so PMs can evaluate tradeoffs.
infra-bot: [sim-update] sim-leasewise-1874021123 started (workers=6). ETA ~45m.
Kai: For fairness index, I can write a small eval that computes Jain's index per 5m buckets and a percentile delta heatmap.
Mateo: I'll add hooks to trace origin (region/az) — want to ensure we don't bias tenants in multi-region setups. If a tenant's traffic fans out across regions, their lease accounting must be global or at least coordinated.
Jess: Also check cross-tenant priority tiers (free vs paid). The controller must respect hard overrides for enterprise SLAs.
Anna: yep — base_credit will be bumped for enterprise tenants via simple multiplier and ignored for throttling until penalty_threshold. We'll encode that in config.
Mateo: Any objections to running sim with two variants: one where leases are strictly local (per pool) and one where leases are federated across pools? Compare fairness and cross-region latency.
Kai: No objections. That comparison is important.
Jess: Who will own the sim analysis and write up? Anna? Mateo?
Anna: I can pick up initial analysis and share a short doc in #eng-infra within 24h after sim completes. Mateo and Kai can add fairness/cross-region sections.
